summary: Verified Strava OAuth APP_URL fallback fix. Backend: GET /api/strava/connect returns 200 with a valid Strava authorize URL (redirect_uri ends in /api/strava/callback, HTTPS). Subprocess test confirms server.APP_URL falls back to PUBLIC_APP_URL when APP_URL is truly absent. Frontend: admin login on 390x844, Rides tab auto-shown, strava-panel renders strava-sync state (already connected), fetch to /api/strava/connect returns 200 with a valid Strava URL, zero JS errors. As noted by main agent, preview redirect_uri still contains the stale OS-env APP_URL host — not flagged as a bug.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py calls load_dotenv() with default override=False, so a stale OS-level APP_URL will always beat backend/.env — main agent knows this; leaving as-is per instruction.
StravaPanel.jsx renders twice in the DOM (mobile+desktop layout wrappers). Not a bug but duplicated data-testids can confuse selector logic; consider gating with a single mount.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression file /app/backend/tests/test_strava_connect.py has 2 tests: (1) live /api/strava/connect returns 200 with valid URL, (2) subprocess import with APP_URL unset and PUBLIC_APP_URL set proves fallback. The subprocess sets cwd=/tmp to prevent server.py's load_dotenv() from picking up backend/.env, and copies only non-APP_URL keys from backend/.env into the child env. Preview redirect_uri shows the stale preview host (known, per main agent).
rca of the issue: Production APP_URL secret was never set. Previous code raised HTTP 500 when APP_URL was empty. Fix in server.py falls back to PUBLIC_APP_URL (already set to https://greylynncc.com in prod). Verified by subprocess import test and live endpoint test.
